followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain the 12 October 2023 freight strike and reported same-day restoration. Workers’ body-return demand and subsequent assurance are documented. Import/export freight trucks are the affected cohort, with workers and unions imposing the stoppage. The BSF/body-return dispute does not make this a state-ordered passenger closure. Both dates remain 12 October. Jago’s eight-hour and Ajker’s nine-hour accounts conflict, while the English report is ongoing. Same-day restoration is retained with numeric duration and exact operational flags withheld. Rights/other-policy-grievance coding follows the stated demand to return the deceased driver’s body. No protectionist purpose is inferred. Jago was freshly read; the other two reports and two geographic sources were reused. Shared union/port spokespeople are not independent reconstruction, and the map source is not event evidence. The B01 approved approximate point exactly matches OSM node 7557117257 version 3: latitude 23.0379104, longitude 88.8839323. LPAI confirms crossing identity. Preserve freight-only scope and day-marker rule; this is not a barricade coordinate or passenger-denial claim.
